brave_no_key.ask_every_time_detail: Off (the default): Jarvis asks first only when private things could slip into a search - after it has read your email, files, notes, saved memories or other outside text - and shows you the exact search words. On: it asks before every search. Turning this on is immediate; turning it off asks you with an approval card.
brave_no_key.default_why: SearXNG is the default because it costs nothing, needs no key or account, and runs on this PC, so no single search company keeps a record of your searches.
brave_no_key.key_entry: Keys are entered on the PC only - in the desktop app's Settings, Web search, or with one line in PowerShell (backend/README.md). The phone never asks for one: sending a key to the PC would send it somewhere other than its own service.

left_out.label: Whoogle
left_out.why: Not offered: its own README says it no longer returns results, since Google blocked searching without JavaScript in 2025.

providers.label: SearXNG (on this PC)
providers.why: Free, no key and no account: a search program that runs on this PC in Docker and asks several search engines for you, without their cookies or trackers. Those engines still see your internet address, and it needs Docker plus one setting (JSON) switched on.

providers.label: DuckDuckGo
providers.said: The DuckDuckGo search needs the ddgs package, which is not installed on this PC. Install it with one line in PowerShell: py -3 -m pip install ddgs
providers.why: Free, no key, and only one Python package to install (ddgs). It reads DuckDuckGo's public pages because there is no official way in, so it can be slowed down or stop working when DuckDuckGo changes, and DuckDuckGo still sees your internet address.

providers.label: Exa
providers.said: No Exa key is saved on this PC. Add it in the desktop app's Settings, Web search (get one at https://dashboard.exa.ai (sign up, then API Keys)).
providers.why: Finds pages by meaning, not just matching words, and returns the useful passages of each page, with about $10 of free credit a month (roughly 1,400 searches) and no payment card. Needs a free account and a key, and Exa sees what you search, tied to your key.

providers.label: Tavily

providers.why: Made for AI assistants: short, clean results, with 1,000 free credits a month (a basic search uses one). Needs a free account and a key, and Tavily sees what you search, tied to your key.

left_out.label: Whoogle
left_out.why: Not offered: its own README says it no longer returns results, since Google blocked searching without JavaScript in 2025.

why.brave: Brave's own independent index, with about $5 of free credit each month (roughly 1,000 searches). Needs an account, a payment card that is charged if you go past the free credit, and a key, and Brave sees what you search, tied to your key.
why.duckduckgo: Free, no key, and only one Python package to install (ddgs). It reads DuckDuckGo's public pages because there is no official way in, so it can be slowed down or stop working when DuckDuckGo changes, and DuckDuckGo still sees your internet address.
why.exa: Finds pages by meaning, not just matching words, and returns the useful passages of each page, with about $10 of free credit a month (roughly 1,400 searches) and no payment card. Needs a free account and a key, and Exa sees what you search, tied to your key.
why.searxng: Free, no key and no account: a search program that runs on this PC in Docker and asks several search engines for you, without their cookies or trackers. Those engines still see your internet address, and it needs Docker plus one setting (JSON) switched on.
why.tavily: Made for AI assistants: short, clean results, with 1,000 free credits a month (a basic search uses one). Needs a free account and a key, and Tavily sees what you search, tied to your key.
